newsitem.title: CHINA: Cambodia's Sihanouk urges end to torture, killing.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Sihanouk urges end to torture, killing.

text.p: Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk on Tuesday accused the police and army of Second Prime Minister Hun Sen of torturing and killing political opponents and urged an end to the bloodshed.

King Sihanouk, in a letter sent from Beijing to acting head of state Chea Sim in Phnom Penh, insisted his neutrality in the conflict between the second prime minister and his son, First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, who was deposed in a bloody coup this month.

"I am profoundly distressed at the reports that that the military and members of the national police have cruelly tortured and killed without mercy their enemies after having arrested or captured them," Sihanouk said.

The king's message followed reports from Phnom Penh on Monday quoting Western officials as saying at least 25 people have been killed in custody since Hun Sen seized power in Phnom Penh on July 6. Some of those allegedly killed were reportedly tortured first.
The king, who reigns but does not rule in Cambodia, reminded the government in Cambodia that the law and the constitution absolutely forbid torture and murder.
"Our Cambodia is officially a liberal democracy," Sihanouk said in the letter issued from his residence in Beijing where he has been undergoing medical treatment.
"In such a democracy, the accused have... the right to a lawyer to defend them," he said.

Hundreds of supporters and soldiers loyal to Prince Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party are believed to remain in detention, although officials of Hun Sen's former communist Cambodian People's Party (CPP) have disputed reported figures and denied allegations of mistreatment.

Sihanouk urged that those detained or arrested as enemies of the state should be treated in line with the law, as well as in accordance with provisions of relevant international treaties to which Cambodia is a signatory state.
"If we regard the current situation in Cambodia as a state of war, we must properly abide by the Geneva Convention provisions relating to treatment of prisoners of war," he said.
Sihanouk stressed his own neutrality in the crisis.
"I take no side with my son," he said.
However, the king said he felt compelled to intervene because under Cambodia's constitution he is the protector of the rights and freedoms of all citizens and the guarantor of international treaties.
Chea Sim is president of the National Assembly and nominal leader of the CPP, whose forces have seized control of Phnom Penh and most of the rest of Cambodia from those loyal to FUNCINPEC.

Hun Sen has said international human rights organisations could check the human rights situation in his country. The London-based human rights group Amnesty International has expressed grave fears for the safety of detainees picked up after Ranariddhs's ouster.
Three foreign ministers of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) are to fly into Beijing to meet King Sihanouk on Thursday to try to seek a solution to the Cambodian crisis.
Indonesia's Ali Alatas would leave for the Chinese capital on Wednesday night and meet up with the Thai and Philippines foreign ministers there.
The ASEAN nations have mandated Alatas and foreign ministers Prachuab Chaiyasarn of Thailand and Domingo Siazon of the Philippines to meet Sihanouk to try to promote a negotiated settlement.
